purpose: Mitotane is used to treat a type of cancer that forms in the adrenal glands, called adrenocortical carcinoma. It can also help control symptoms caused by too many hormones being made by the adrenal glands. Your doctor may use it alone or along with other treatments.
how_it_works: Your adrenal glands sit on top of your kidneys and make important hormones. Mitotane works by directly attacking and damaging the adrenal gland tissue so it makes fewer harmful hormones and cancer cells are destroyed. Think of it as a targeted medicine that zeroes in on adrenal tissue to slow or stop cancer growth.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and loss of appetite are very common, especially when starting the medicine. Many people also feel very tired, dizzy, or confused, and may have trouble with coordination or walking steadily. Skin rashes and muscle aches can also happen.
warnings: Because mitotane suppresses your adrenal glands, your body may not make enough stress hormones, which can be life-threatening — especially during illness, surgery, or injury. You will likely need to take steroid replacement medicines while on mitotane. Avoid driving or operating machinery if you feel dizzy or confused. Women who are pregnant or planning to become pregnant must not take this medicine, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Always carry a medical alert card letting others know you are on this medication.
typical_dosing: Dosing is very individual and based on blood levels of the drug. It is usually started at a low dose, around 2 to 6 grams per day taken by mouth in divided doses, and gradually increased up to 9 to 10 grams per day or sometimes higher as tolerated. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to find the right dose that is effective but safe for you.
